title: Pittsburgh Home Rebates 2026: Duquesne Light Pause and Free Weatherization
desc: Pittsburgh home rebates in 2026: Duquesne Light's rebate store is closed between rounds, free weatherization through ACTION-Housing, the state's Penn Energy Savers launch, and what ended.
lead: Pittsburgh is between rounds. Duquesne Light's rebate store said on October 5, 2026 that energy rebates are not available yet while the next round is built, and the state's big federal-funded rebate program has not launched either. What is open today is free weatherization for income-eligible households, plus Pennsylvania's net metering for solar. Here is how to plan around it for the city's 138,188 occupied homes.
cards_heading: What is open for Pittsburgh homes in 2026
cards_intro: Each card names the fact we keep on file, with the date we last read the official page. We show no Duquesne Light dollar amount because the utility does not publish one right now.

cards.title: Duquesne Light rebates
cards.note: The rebate store says energy rebates are not available yet while the next round is brought online. Call 1-888-928-8539 for the start date.

cards.title: Penn Energy Savers
cards.note: The state's federal-funded HOMES and HEEHR rebates have no launch date or published amounts. The state is revising the design after new federal guidance in June 2026.

cards.title: ACTION-Housing weatherization
cards.note: Air sealing, insulation and heating work for households at or below 200% of poverty, in the City of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County.

cards.title: State Weatherization Assistance Program
cards.note: The state program behind ACTION-Housing's work. The state reports an average spend of $8,547 per household.

cards.title: Net metering for solar
cards.note: Systems up to 50 kW are credited at the full retail rate for the power they send to the grid. This is a policy, not a cash rebate.

cards.title: PA Sunshine Solar Program
cards.note: The state solar rebate stopped taking applications in 2013.

cards.title: Federal 25C and 25D credits
cards.note: No federal credit applies to work done after December 31, 2025.

sections: Why we list no Duquesne Light amount

Duquesne Light's own website showed a security check when our reader visited, and we do not get past those. Its rebate store, run by a contractor, loaded and says plainly that rebates are not available yet. Sites that still quote Duquesne Light dollar amounts are quoting older figures. We will not print them as if they were open. When the store reopens, the amounts will come from that page.

The Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) counts 161,908 homes in Pittsburgh. Detached houses are the biggest group at 43.6%, followed by 14.5% in buildings of two to four units and 14.1% attached homes. Pittsburgh has the oldest stock of the four Pennsylvania cities we cover on one measure: 48.3% of homes were built before 1940, and 83.0% before 1980. Only 9.6% date from 2000 or later.

Gas heats 75.2% of households, electricity 21.0%, bottled gas 1.9% and fuel oil only 0.6%. Because oil is nearly absent, the oil-to-heat-pump switch that matters in Allentown is rare here. The better targets are the roughly one in five homes on electric heat, and any house whose old furnace is due. Renters are 52.3% of households, so many Pittsburgh decisions belong to a landlord.
Free weatherization is the open door

ACTION-Housing runs the state weatherization program for the City of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County. It is free for owners, and for renters with a landlord's sign-off, whose income is at or below 200% of poverty. The 2025 limits on its page are $30,300 for one person, $42,300 for two, $53,300 for three and $64,300 for four, with $11,000 for each extra person. You need three months in the home and your gas and electric bills. No lien is placed on the property. To ask for an application, call 412-281-2102.

If your furnace has died, do not wait for Duquesne Light. A dead heating system cannot wait. If you can plan, watch the rebate store before you buy. We do not know the next round's rules or dates, so keep the paid invoice and ask your installer for the model numbers and AHRI certificate in writing, in case you can claim later.

Pittsburgh's average January low is about -5.1°C (22°F), and the coldest reading in our ten years of data was -29.2°C, the lowest of our four Pennsylvania cities. Choose a cold-climate heat pump and ask how the system handles those nights.
installers_intro: Ranked by Google reviews (minimum five). We don't take referral fees or paid placements. Ask each installer whether they have worked under Duquesne Light's rebate program before.
claim_steps: Check your income against ACTION-Housing's limits. If you qualify, request a weatherization application.
Call Duquesne Light on 1-888-928-8539 and ask when its rebate store reopens.
If you must replace equipment now, get the model numbers and AHRI certificate in writing.
Keep every paid invoice for the next round.
Join the update list on pennenergysavers.com for the state program.
faq: Does Duquesne Light pay for a heat pump in 2026?
Not right now. Its rebate store says energy rebates are not available yet while the next round is brought online. We list no amount until it publishes one.
Is there free help in Pittsburgh?
Yes. ACTION-Housing runs the state weatherization program for the City of Pittsburgh and Allegheny County, free for households at or below 200% of the federal poverty level.
When will Penn Energy Savers open?
The state has not said. DEP says it is changing the design after new federal guidance from June 1, 2026, and it publishes no launch date or rebate amounts.
Is there a solar rebate in Pittsburgh?
No cash rebate. The PA Sunshine program closed in 2013 and the federal credit ended after 2025. Pennsylvania does credit solar exports at the retail rate for systems up to 50 kW.
Can I claim the federal heat pump credit?
No. Federal credits for heat pumps, insulation, solar and batteries ended for spending after December 31, 2025.
